task.title: Verify table cell text alignment in the Web Editor
task.shortdesc: Use this task to validate acceptance criteria for applying text alignment to table cells from the context menu, including published output and cross-browser behavior.

li.p: You can open and edit a DITA topic in Experience Manager Guides Web Editor.
A topic is available that contains at least one table with one or more cells you can select.
For cross-browser verification, install or have access to current versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

context.p: This procedure confirms that authors can align text inside a table cell using the context menu, that alignment is reflected in output (HTML and DITA), and that existing table configuration workflows still work.

note.p: These steps map to acceptance criteria for the table cell text alignment feature: context menu options, immediate application without opening the table properties dialog for the alignment action, output consistency, browser coverage, and regression on the table properties dialog.

step.cmd: Right-click inside a table cell and confirm that the context menu includes a Text Alignment submenu.

info.p: Open the submenu and verify the following options are available: Left, Center, Right, and Justify.

step.cmd: Select each alignment option in turn and confirm the active cell updates immediately.

info.p: You should not need to open the table properties dialog solely to apply the alignment chosen from the context menu.

step.cmd: Verify that the chosen alignment is preserved in output and in source as specified for your pipeline.

info.p: For HTML-oriented output, inspect that alignment is reflected appropriately (for example via a style attribute on the relevant element).
For DITA source, inspect that alignment is represented with an align attribute (or equivalent supported markup) on the appropriate table cell element.

step.cmd: Repeat the context menu alignment checks in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

info.p: Behavior should be consistent: the submenu appears, options apply, and the cell reflects the selected alignment in each browser.

step.cmd: Open the existing table properties dialog for the same table and confirm it still opens, saves, and applies settings as before.

info.p: This confirms no regression for authors who continue to use the table properties workflow for other table options.

li.p: The Text Alignment submenu and four alignment options appear from the cell context menu.
Alignment applies immediately without requiring the table properties dialog for that action.
Published or previewed HTML reflects alignment (for example via style), and DITA source uses align (or your supported equivalent).
The same behavior works in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
The table properties dialog continues to function for table configuration.
